title: Placing Primary School Students Taking Subjects at Foundation Level in Same Class as Other Students to Ensure Social Mixing
what_it_is: Placing Primary School Students Taking Subjects at Foundation Level in Same Class as Other Students to Ensure Social Mixing

sections.label: Primary school foundation level class mixing
sections.summary: Asked whether Primary students taking foundation subjects can be placed in the same class as others to ensure social mixing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether Primary school students taking subjects at a foundation level can be placed in the same class as students who are not taking foundation level subjects to ensure social mixing, similar to that in Secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Thus, form classes at Primary 5 and 6 can have students of several subject combinations, including a mix of students taking subjects at Foundation and Standard levels.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Beyond classes, students also have opportunities to interact with their peers through school-wide platforms such as Co-Curricular Activities (CCAs).

sections.label: Grouping Primary 5 form classes
sections.summary: Students are grouped in Primary 5 form classes after Primary 4 tests determine whether they take Foundation or Standard level subjects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Yes, as I mentioned, we do group students in form classes at Primary 5, because at Primary 4, they take tests to ascertain their competency level and they are allowed to then decide based on consultation with their parents, too, on the subject level that they are prepared to take – whether it is at Foundation or at the Standard level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Some students do take one or two subjects at the Foundation level, depending on their level of abilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: When allocating students to classes, schools aim to create an inclusive and caring learning environment, so as to nurture and develop students holistically.

sections.label: Class grouping considerations and flexibility
sections.summary: Considerations include common subjects for bonding, teacher capability with wide abilities and resource limitations, with schools given flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: But there are certain considerations, given the class size that we have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: These considerations include having enough common subjects for the form class to bond but it also depends on the capability of teachers with a wide range of abilities and resource limitations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Schools are given flexibility to manage and operationalise the groupings.

sections.label: Social mixing one consideration
sections.summary: Social mixing is one of many considerations in how students are grouped in classes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Social mixing is but one of the many considerations in how students are grouped in classes.
